title: QUIC and HTTP/3 behind ZIA: where it escapes and how to block it

cert-errors.statement: Zscaler cannot examine QUIC sessions when SSL/TLS Inspection is on, and users may also see certificate errors when QUIC is used.

quotes: Because of this, Zscaler cannot examine QUIC sessions when users have SSL/TLS Inspection enabled. When using QUIC, users might also experience certificate errors.

tunnel2-firewall-rule.statement: For traffic arriving through a GRE or IPSec tunnel, or Client Connector with Z-Tunnel 2.0, QUIC is blocked with a Firewall Filtering rule on the QUIC network service, which forces the browser back to TCP 80 and 443. Z-Tunnel 2.0 can send all ports and protocols.

quotes: you can effectively block QUIC by creating a Firewall Filtering rule. This blocks QUIC UDP flows and forces the browser to default to TCP 80/443.
Z-Tunnel 2.0 is capable of sending all ports and protocols.

default-rule-blocks.statement: The default Firewall Filtering rule (lowest rank) normally blocks QUIC unless it is specifically allowed, but admin-created permissive rules above it often let QUIC through, so a QUIC block rule may need to precede them.

quotes: Normally, the default Firewall Filtering Rule (the lowest rank rule) blocks QUIC unless specifically allowed.
one or more QUIC block rules might be needed to precede admin-defined allow rules.

udp-80.statement: QUIC can use UDP destination port 80 as well as 443, so the predefined QUIC network service has to be modified, or a custom service created, to cover both.

quotes: In addition to UDP destination port 443, QUIC can use UDP destination port 80.

tunnel1-device-firewall.statement: For Client Connector traffic on Z-Tunnel 1.0 (which sends only proxy-aware or port 80 and 443 traffic), the block belongs on the device firewall: UDP 80 and 443.

quotes: create a block rule on your device firewall to block UDP 80 and 443.
Z-Tunnel 1.0 sends all proxy-aware traffic or port 80/443 traffic to the Zscaler service

tunnel1-udp-leaves.statement: So under Z-Tunnel 1.0, or any TCP 80 and 443 only forwarding, QUIC UDP does not reach Zscaler at all: it leaves the device directly and is neither inspected nor blocked by a Zscaler Firewall Filtering rule.
tunnel1-udp-leaves.conditions: Inference from Help directing the block to the device or branch firewall; the legacy phrasing "egresses outside the tunnel" is not in a source.

tcp-only-branch.statement: If only TCP 80 and 443 go over the tunnel to Zscaler, QUIC is blocked on the branch firewall.

quotes: If you are only sending TCP 80/443 over a tunnel to Zscaler, block QUIC on your branch firewall.

dns-https-records.statement: QUIC can also be discouraged with a DNS Control rule that blocks the HTTPS resource record type with a Server Failure response, because browsers use those records to choose HTTP/3 and the Zscaler web proxy does not support HTTP/3.

quotes: Zscaler recommends configuring your DNS Control policy to block HTTPS resource records to suppress the use of HTTP/3 over QUIC

conferencing-media.title: Webex and Teams media over Z-Tunnel 2.0 and process-based bypass
conferencing-media.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "The canonical case where this matters: WebEx media (UDP 9000 SRTP, fallback TCP 443) and Microsoft Teams call quality. If Z-Tunnel 2.0 captures the media flow, voice/video degrades. Process-based bypass of the conferencing client is the documented pattern." The captured Z-Tunnel and QUIC pages do not mention Webex or Teams media; the captured Advanced Policy Settings page covers a UCaaS One Click option for Zoom, GoTo, RingCentral, Webex and Talkdesk, not Teams media.
